evidence: DeformX models DLOs as Cosserat rods; the framework is a direct application of Cosserat rod theory.
Rod engine uses a discrete Cosserat formulation in the Bergou-Audoly DER family (vertices + per-edge SO(3) frames).
Object class targeted by the framework.
Sim-to-real transfer of policies trained in DeformX is the paper's central empirical claim.
Paper proposes the multi-rate Cosserat-rod + Isaac Sim co-simulation pattern; this is the paper's primary architectural contribution.
Rope-swinging hit-target task on UR5e: DeformX vs. Isaac linked-capsule baseline reduces real-world tip-to-goal error from 15.1/25.9/30.4 cm to 6.6/7.3/5.8 cm across three targets, n=10 each.
RopeDreamer's target object class is the DLO (rope, cable, suture); the paper formalizes the DLO state and dynamics modeling task.
Forward kinematics with fixed link length is used to recover Cartesian segment positions from the quaternionic kinematic-chain state representation.
RSSM (Recurrent State Space Model) is the canonical world-model backbone from the Dreamer/PlaNet line of model-based RL, adapted here as a DLO dynamics model.

Paper introduces the Quaternionic Kinematic RSSM with dual-decoder architecture combining quaternion-based DLO state representation, RSSM latent dynamics, and separate reconstruction/prediction decoders.

MuJoCo benchmark over 500 50-step rollouts: 40.52% RMSE reduction at t=50 vs. GA-Net S baseline, 31.17% inference-time reduction; topology fidelity (Gauss-code) holds 38-65% across horizon while baselines drop below 10% by t=30; ablation isolates long-horizon stability to RSSM rather than the quaternionic representation alone.
